clue.text: Insubstantial small muscle lacks oxygen

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: lacks says the muscle word goes without one of its letters here

parts.note: a pectoral is a chest muscle
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A puny little muscle starved of oxygen sounds like a gym-goer's complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacks' signals the deletion; the chest muscle is the one losing a letter, giving PECTRAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spectral is ghostly, a phantom without physical substance.

clue.text: See 9
Desirable person's improper message about urine container

indicators.note: about means the message word is wrapped around the container word

parts.note: a sext is a sexually explicit text message
a po is a chamber pot

explanation.surface: Someone attractive sends a rude text mentioning a chamber pot, an unlikely seduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'po' is an old British word for a chamber pot; 'about' signals the wrapping, and the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexpot is slang for a person regarded as sexually alluring.

clue.text: Appeal to leaders of African tribal region

indicators.note: leaders of asks for the opening letters of the two words that follow

parts.note: a tract is an area or region of land

explanation.surface: A plea addressed to the chiefs of an African tribal area.
explanation.definitionFit: To attract someone is to appeal to them, a straightforward synonym in verb form.

clue.text: Round book printed on dedicated computer paper

parts.note: O is round in shape
a server is a computer dedicated to providing services to a network

explanation.surface: Seems to describe printing a book on a networked computer's paper supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'printed on' is a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper, so a paper in the press sense.

clue.text: Is the Queen unable to cover an old music stand?

parts.note: can't means unable to
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
to bury something is to cover it over

explanation.surface: Asks whether Her Majesty is incapable of hiding an antique stand for sheet music.
explanation.definitionFit: A canterbury is a period piece of furniture, a low rack for holding sheet music or magazines.

clue.text: Wood and metal off the boat

parts.note: ash is a timber tree
ore is rock from which metal is extracted

explanation.surface: Cargo of timber and metal unloaded from a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on land, i.e. having disembarked from a vessel.

clue.text: Seeming to turn old man against old man?

indicators.note: to turn tells us the first father word is read backwards

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
one's old man is one's father, a parent

explanation.surface: Appears to describe one father being set against another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' reverses PA; 'against' just sets the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent means seeming, as in an apparent success that is not real.

clue.text: Cheap wedding ring that plays tunes

definitions.meaning: a ... of ... rather than gold would be a cheap wedding ring
a group of musicians playing tunes

explanation.surface: A tawdry ring for a wedding that somehow also plays music.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass band is an ensemble of brass instruments that performs music; literally, a ring of brass is a cheap band.

clue.text: Sweet things like to embrace detectives and dribble

indicators.note: to embrace has the comparison word wrapping around what follows

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives
a drop is a small dribble of liquid

explanation.surface: Sugary treats that apparently hug police officers and make them drool.
explanation.walkthrough: AS opens to take CID and DROP: A(CIDDROP)S.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid drops are sharp-tasting boiled sweets, popular British confectionery.

clue.text: Understanding exercise function requires no energy

parts.note: PE is physical education

indicators.note: requires no says one letter is dropped from the function word

parts.note: a reception is a social function
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A dry statement about workouts and efficiency, as if from a physics lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requires no' signals the deletion of one E, leaving RCEPTION; PE is British school shorthand for physical education.
explanation.definitionFit: Perception is insight or comprehension, a synonym for understanding.

clue.text: Crossword started (bloody Brummie!) — time to have belief

indicators.note: started points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: blood is red
Brummie is the setter, so from the setter's view this is I

explanation.surface: The setter curses himself while a solver takes a moment to trust the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by their pseudonym, giving I or ME.
explanation.definitionFit: To give credit to a story is to believe it, so credit means belief or trust.

clue.text: Analysis of Pluto zone

parts.note: Dis is another name for Pluto, Roman god of the underworld
a section is a zone or area

explanation.surface: Seems to be an astronomer's study of a region of the dwarf planet.
explanation.walkthrough: Pluto here is the god, not the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissection is a detailed examination, figuratively a close analysis.

clue.text: Bedding etc unfortunately restricts active lover

indicators.note: restricts means the first jumble hems in the second
unfortunately suggests things gone awry, so the three letters are shuffled
active suggests movement, so the letters of the lover word are stirred

explanation.surface: Sheets and so on that sadly cramp an energetic lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'etc' looks like a throwaway abbreviation but is fodder for 'unfortunately'; 'active' shuffles the lover, and 'restricts' hems that jumble inside the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A coverlet is a bedspread, a type of bedding.

clue.text: Get high on your own smart performance

parts.note: fly is slang for sharp or smart
a solo is a performance by one person

explanation.surface: Sounds like advice on taking drugs alone before a clever show.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly solo is to pilot an aircraft alone, i.e. go up in the air unaccompanied.

clue.text: Affectedly well-read, or else excited about it

indicators.note: about has the jumbled letters going around the following word
excited suggests agitation, so the letters of or else are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pretentious bookworm getting worked up over something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' makes LEROSE from the letters of or else, and 'about' sets it around the word it.
explanation.definitionFit: Literose describes someone who parades their literary learning, pretentiously bookish.

clue.text: Sediment area around house

definitions.meaning: the ... of a house are its surrounding land

explanation.definitionFit: Grounds means both settled particles in a liquid and the estate surrounding a building.

clue.text: Unmissable date — and phone not working?

definitions.meaning: a time limit that must be met
a ... is a telephone line with no signal

explanation.definitionFit: A deadline is a must-meet cut-off; read as two words, a dead line describes a silent telephone.

clue.text: University, rather unorthodox, that's used by a peer

definitions.note: a definition by description: the thing one who pees uses

indicators.note: unorthodox means departing from the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Suggests a college with odd customs frequented by a member of the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'peer' as 'pee-er', someone urinating, not a lord.
explanation.definitionFit: The urethra is the duct through which urine leaves the body, so anyone urinating uses it.

clue.text: Bird's bill, cornet-shaped

parts.note: AC, for account, is a bill

indicators.note: shaped means formed into a new arrangement, so the instrument's letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A bird whose beak looks like a small trumpet.
explanation.walkthrough: CORNET rearranged gives CENTOR; the 's is a link ("is").
explanation.definitionFit: The accentor is a small songbird, the dunnock being the best-known example.

clue.text: Dull city centre's gone flashy inside

indicators.note: inside places the flashy word within what remains
centre's gone says the middle letters of the place word are dropped

parts.note: loud means showy or garish, as in loud clothes

explanation.surface: A boring town whose core has been lost to garish development.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre's gone' strips the middle pair from the place word, leaving CY; 'inside' then puts the flashy word within.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloudy weather is dull and overcast.

clue.text: Having a particular way of removing outer bits from crusty larvae

indicators.note: removing outer bits from strips the ends off the two words so the inner letters remain

explanation.surface: Reads like a recipe or a naturalist's method of peeling crusty grubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop C, RU from the front and VAE from the back of 'crusty larvae'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylar means relating to a style, i.e. a distinctive manner, so possessing a particular way.

clue.text: Swipe church sample

parts.note: to swat is to strike with a swipe

explanation.surface: Someone pinches an example from a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swipe' suggests stealing; here it means a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A swatch is a small piece of fabric used as a sample.

clue.text: Britten composition found inside Bird's plant

indicators.note: found inside sets the jumble within the bird

parts.note: the moa is an extinct flightless New Zealand bird

indicators.note: composition means putting together anew, so the composer's name is rearranged

explanation.surface: A Britten piece discovered within a bird's plant, nicely musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' makes NTBRETI from the composer's name, and 'found inside' splits the extinct bird around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Montbretia is a flowering garden plant (crocosmia) with orange blooms.

clue.text: Chamber is consequently filled by island lake

indicators.note: filled by means the first word is stuffed with what follows

parts.note: so means consequently, therefore

explanation.surface: A room is thereby occupied by an isle and a lake, a geographic oddity.
explanation.definitionFit: A silo is a storage chamber, for grain or for missiles.

clue.text: Lacking source of education, looks up 'beehive'

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters read upwards, i.e. backwards
lacking says a letter is removed from the looks word

parts.note: peeks are quick looks

indicators.note: source of points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An uneducated person searches out the word beehive.
explanation.walkthrough: PEEKS less E is PEKS; 'up' reverses it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A skep is a traditional straw or wicker beehive.

clue.text: See 10
Withdraw, carrying emptied rifle, being cowardly

indicators.note: carrying means the first word holds the second within it

parts.note: to recant is to withdraw a statement

indicators.note: emptied means the word is cleared of its insides, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A soldier retreating with an unloaded gun, hardly a hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emptied' leaves just the outer letters of rifle; 'carrying' puts them inside the word for withdraw. 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Recreant is an archaic adjective for craven, lacking courage.
